newHazards.detail:
`refundEstimateReason` is not prose: priceReturn's only refusal value is the literal `"NOTHING_CREDITABLE"` (returns.service.ts:487, :510), passed through unchanged as `refusal ?? null` by findAll (:282) and findOne (:810). The resolve modal prints it straight into the DOM — `{showEstimateReason &&

{refundEstimateReason}

}` — so an operator resolving a return on an order whose invoices are all VOID/WRITTEN_OFF gets a SCREAMING_SNAKE enum token where the ruling asked for one muted explanatory line. The gating logic is right and the field plumbing is right; only the copy layer is missing. Two one-line options: map the token to prose on the client (a `Record` beside `fmtMoney`, falling back to the raw value so a future token still says something), or have the api emit the sentence and keep the token for machines. Prefer whichever keeps the api's value machine-readable, since the field is documented as the thing that distinguishes a refusal from a genuine $0.

review.reasoning:
All seven in-scope findings (0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8) are genuinely fixed — I tried to refute each by tracing its own failure_scenario through the current tree and could not break any of them. The strongest confirmations: finding 2's new guard is algebraically identical to the credit-notes cap it models (`amount > total - existing + 0.001` vs `existing + amount > total + 0.001`, same epsilon, same VOID/invoiceId scope), so it converts a post-claim throw into a pre-claim refusal without ever over-refusing; finding 5's `!= null` genuinely preserves the dto.reason fallback, which the pre-existing pin at returns-overreturn.spec.ts:294 still proves green; finding 4's `extrasReady` is unchanged and still blocks on pending, with refetch hitting only errored entries; finding 7's parity spec fails on a change to EITHER side and fails loudly (not vacuously) on a rename or a shape change, following enum-parity.spec.ts's own precedent. Findings 3, 6 and 9 are code-untouched — the only motion near 6 is the headroom block moving inside an explicit `if (creditable.length >= 2)`, which runs on exactly the input set the old `< 2` early return already gave it.

What stops me recommending land is one major hazard the round created by composition. `invoiceNumber` is not in processRefund's invoice select, so the per-invoice refusal names a raw UUID — and this round both widened that message to the common single-invoice path (finding 2) and routed it straight to the operator's toast (finding 0). The naming of the invoice was the entire point of finding 0's ruling, and it is the one part that does not survive to production. Worse, the round's own pin asserts `/INV-060/` against a fixture that supplies a field the real query never fetches, so the suite reports confidence it has not earned. That is precisely the class of defect a refute-first pass exists to stop, and it is a one-line fix (`invoiceNumber: true` at returns.service.ts:572), after which the existing fixture and assertion become honest with no spec edit. Pair it with the second hazard — the modal printing `NOTHING_CREDITABLE` verbatim, also a one-line copy fix — and the round is roughly four lines from landing clean, both inside files this round already owns and both re-gated by the same two api commands plus the web tsc.

Two residuals for the close-out rather than another round: the cross-side coupling on the api's \"exceeds remaining returnable\" prose is still unpinned (the mobile test hand-copies the string, so a server reword leaves both sides green) — round 3 has now established the static-scan technique that would close it; and mobile's local `Return` type carries `refundEstimate` but not `refundEstimateReason`, harmless today only because no mobile screen renders the estimate at all.
